records.context: **Two keys answer this one question, and both are honoured.** The Animation preference gained a ``None`` entry (see :data:`spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.NO_ANIMATION`), and "no animation" has to mean *nothing is constructed* rather than "an engine that paints an empty frame sixty times a second". The three install sites all read this function before they build anything, so answering ``False`` for None here is what makes the guarantee true everywhere at once, without a second condition in three other modules that could drift apart.

records.source: **Two keys answer this one question, and both are honoured.** The Animation preference gained a ``None`` entry (see :data:`spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.NO_ANIMATION`), and "no animation" has to mean *nothing is constructed* rather than "an engine that paints an empty frame sixty times a second". The three install sites all read this function before they build anything, so answering ``False`` for None here is what makes the guarantee true everywhere at once, without a second condition in three other modules that could drift apart.
records.translation: **Tveir lyklar svara þessari einu spurningu, og báðir eru virtir.** Animation-stillingin fékk ``None``-færslu (sjá :data:`spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.NO_ANIMATION`), og "no animation" verður að þýða að *ekkert sé smíðað* frekar en "an engine that paints an empty frame sixty times a second". records.context: Read by :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue.render_figure_to_png`, which is the single consumer. ``pdf`` makes it write a vector page beside the display raster; the work list then rasterises that page for a crisper view and the user has a file that opens as editable art. Scope is worth stating, since the name suggests otherwise: this is the format of the figures spaCR renders **for its own Figures panel**. records.context: What this reaches and what it does not. It is the colour of the figure's CHROME: the axis spines and the tick marks. It is deliberately not pushed over the data's own lines on every render, because a preference that repainted every series in one ink would flatten every multi-series figure in the package the first time a theme was read. The control that DOES reach the data's lines is the per-figure one (:func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_settings.apply_line_colour`), which is a user asking for it about one figure -- the same division as the pyqtgraph side, where the theme sets `_foreground` and `set_line_colour` is a menu entry.

records.context: Two consumers, and they treat it differently on purpose. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue.render_figure_to_png` clamps it for the on-application view raster — a 16x12" figure at 300 DPI is a 4800 px PNG that costs more to decode than any application view can show — so a large figure is displayed at a lower DPI than the one chosen here. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue._export_vector_pdf` uses the value unclamped, because the PDF is a file rather than a screenful and its embedded rasters really do need the resolution the user asked for.

records.source: Two consumers, and they treat it differently on purpose. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue.render_figure_to_png` clamps it for the on-screen raster — a 16x12" figure at 300 DPI is a 4800 px PNG that costs more to decode than any screen can show — so a large figure is displayed at a lower DPI than the one chosen here. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue._export_vector_pdf` uses the value unclamped, because the PDF is a file rather than a screenful and its embedded rasters really do need the resolution the user asked for.
records.translation: Tveir notendur, og þeir meðhöndla hana ólíkt af ásetningi. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue.render_figure_to_png` takmarkar hana fyrir dílamyndina á skjánum — 16x12" mynd við 300 DPI er 4800 px PNG sem kostar meira að afkóða en nokkur skjár getur sýnt — svo stór mynd er birt með lægri DPI en þeirri sem valin er hér. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue._export_vector_pdf` notar gildið ótakmarkað, því PDF er skrá frekar en skjáfylli og innfelldar dílamyndir hennar þurfa í raun upplausnina sem notandinn bað um.

records.context: 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` must be on — it is off by default and lives in Preferences, not on this screen. 2. The database must have been chosen explicitly in this session (``set_database(..., explicit=True)``). 3. The user must tick "Edit mode" *and* confirm; ticking alone does nothing. 4. The row must be addressable by ``rowid`` or a primary structured-data name. Without one, the edit is refused — an UPDATE matching on column values can hit many rows, which on a measurements table is silent mass corruption. The write also probes ``COUNT(*)`` for the row address first and rolls back unless ``rowcount == 1``. 5. The typed text must be coercible to the column's declared type. SQLite stores ``'abc'`` in an INTEGER column without error; :func:`coerce_for_column` refuses instead.

Without one, the edit is refused — an UPDATE matching on column values can hit many rows, which on a measurements table is silent mass corruption. The write also probes ``COUNT(*)`` for the row address first and rolls back unless ``rowcount == 1``. 5. The typed text must be coercible to the column's declared type. records.translation: 1. Kveikt verður að vera á :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` — slökkt er á því sjálfgefið og það býr í Preferences, ekki í þessu viðmóti. 2. Gagnagrunnurinn verður að hafa verið valinn beint í þessari lotu (``set_database(..., explicit=True)``). 3. Notandinn verður að haka við "Edit mode" *og* staðfesta; að haka eitt og sér gerir ekkert. 4. Línan verður að vera ávarpanleg með ``rowid`` eða aðallykli. Án hans er breytingunni hafnað — UPDATE sem parar á dálkagildum getur hitt margar línur, sem á mælingatöflu er þögul fjöldaspilling. Skrifunin kannar einnig ``COUNT(*)`` fyrir vistfang línunnar fyrst og afturkallar nema ``rowcount == 1``. 5. Innslegni textinn verður að vera umbreytanlegur í uppgefna tegund dálksins. SQLite geymir ``'abc'`` í INTEGER-dálki án villu; :func:`coerce_for_column` hafnar í staðinn.

records.context: **Keyset paging, not OFFSET.** Each chunk asks for ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` and ``ORDER BY rowid``. ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` makes SQLite walk (and throw away) every skipped row, so chunk 500 of a 400 k-row table would cost 500× chunk 1. Only tables with no usable structured-data name (views, composite-primary-structured-data name ``WITHOUT ROWID`` tables) fall back to ``OFFSET``, and those are small by construction.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser#5

records.source: **Keyset paging, not OFFSET.** Each chunk asks for ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` and ``ORDER BY rowid``. ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` makes SQLite walk (and throw away) every skipped row, so chunk 500 of a 400 k-row table would cost 500× chunk 1. Only tables with no usable key (views, composite-primary-key ``WITHOUT ROWID`` tables) fall back to ``OFFSET``, and those are small by construction.
records.translation: **Lyklasíðun, ekki OFFSET.** Hver bútur biður um ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` og ``ORDER BY rowid``. ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` lætur SQLite fara yfir (og henda) hverri línu sem sleppt er, svo bútur 500 í töflu með 400 k línum kostaði 500× bút 1. Aðeins töflur án nothæfs lykils (sýnir, ``WITHOUT ROWID``-töflur með samsettum aðallykli) falla aftur á ``OFFSET``, og þær eru litlar í eðli sínu.

records.context: **The count never blocks the first paint.** ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` is a full scan. The first chunk is painted against ``max(rowid)``, which is O(1), and that number is *always* rendered as "≈… (estimate)". The exact ``COUNT(*)`` follows on its own job and replaces it.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The count never blocks the first paint.** ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` is a full scan. The first chunk is painted against ``max(rowid)``, which is O(1), and that number is *always* rendered as "≈… (estimate)". The exact ``COUNT(*)`` follows on its own job and replaces it.
records.translation: **Talningin hindrar aldrei fyrstu teikningu.** ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` er full skönnun. Fyrsti búturinn er teiknaður miðað við ``max(rowid)``, sem er O(1), og sú tala er *alltaf* birt sem "≈… (estimate)". Nákvæma ``COUNT(*)`` fylgir í eigin verki og kemur í hennar stað.

records.context: **Cancellable.** Switching table or database bumps a load token. Results tagged with a stale token are dropped, so an in-flight load can never paint the previous table's rows into the new view, and a job that has not started yet is dropped without spending an independent execution path. Nothing is ever killed mid-flight.

records.source: **Cancellable.** Switching table or database bumps a load token. records.translation: **Hægt að hætta við.** Að skipta um töflu eða gagnagrunn hækkar hleðslutákn. records.source: the key column is appended as a **tiebreak**. Without it, rows sharing a value come back in whatever order SQLite happens to produce, and that order is free to differ between two chunks of the same scroll -- so a row could be shown twice and another not at all.
records.translation: lykildálkinum er bætt við sem **úrslitaröðun**. Án hans koma línur sem deila gildi til baka í hverri þeirri röð sem SQLite skilar, og sú röð má vera ólík milli tveggja búta sama skruns -- svo lína gæti birst tvisvar og önnur alls ekki.

records.context: **Brush** and **Erase** paint and unpaint the active label a pixel at a time. **Erase object** removes a whole label in one click. **Wand** grows a region from the pixel clicked and adds it to the mask by default. Hold Ctrl while clicking to remove that region; the tolerance is relative to the image's intensity range by default, see :func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.relative_tolerance`. **Draw** traces a free-form outline that closes and fills as ONE object -- the tool a brush is not, because a brush stamps disks along the path, so tracing a rim with it labels the rim and leaves the middle background. **Divide / Merge** uses a left-button drag to divide and a right-button drag to merge crossed objects under the first touched identifier without changing their pixels. The merged identity is retained when saving and reopening. Dividing drags a line across a merged object and makes it two, keeping the original identifier on the larger component and giving the smaller a new one, with every other object untouched; :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.DIVIDE_CUT_WIDTH` is the cut width. **Zoom** rectangle-drags the view and changes no labels at all.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.make_masks#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Brush** and **Erase** paint and unpaint the active label a pixel at a time. **Erase object** removes a whole label in one click. **Wand** grows a region from the pixel clicked and adds it to the mask by default. Hold Ctrl while clicking to remove that region; the tolerance is relative to the image's intensity range by default, see :func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.relative_tolerance`. **Draw** traces a free-form outline that closes and fills as ONE object -- the tool a brush is not, because a brush stamps disks along the path, so tracing a rim with it labels the rim and leaves the middle background. **Divide / Merge** uses a left-button drag to divide and a right-button drag to merge crossed objects under the first touched identifier without changing their pixels. The merged identity is retained when saving and reopening. Dividing drags a line across a merged object and makes it two, keeping the original identifier on the larger component and giving the smaller a new one, with every other object untouched; :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.DIVIDE_CUT_WIDTH` is the cut width. **Zoom** rectangle-drags the view and changes no labels at all.
records.translation: **Brush** og **Erase** mála og afmála virka merkið einn díl í einu. **Erase object** fjarlægir heilt merki með einum smelli. **Wand** stækkar svæði út frá dílnum sem smellt er á og bætir því sjálfgefið við grímuna. Haldið Ctrl niðri meðan smellt er til að fjarlægja það svæði; vikmörkin eru sjálfgefið miðuð við styrkleikasvið myndarinnar, sjá :func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.relative_tolerance`. **Draw** dregur fríhendis útlínu sem lokast og fyllist sem EINN hlutur -- verkfærið sem pensill er ekki, því pensill stimplar skífur eftir leiðinni, svo að draga brún með honum merkir brúnina og skilur miðjuna eftir sem bakgrunn. **Divide / Merge** notar drátt með vinstri hnappi til að skipta og drátt með hægri hnappi til að sameina hluti sem farið er yfir undir auðkenni þess fyrsta sem snert var, án þess að breyta dílum þeirra. Sameinaða auðkennið helst við vistun og enduropnun. Skipting dregur línu þvert yfir sameinaðan hlut og gerir hann að tveimur, heldur upprunalega auðkenninu á stærri þættinum og gefur þeim minni nýtt, án þess að snerta neinn annan hlut; :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.DIVIDE_CUT_WIDTH` er breidd skurðarins. **Zoom** dregur rétthyrning til að þysja sýnina og breytir engum merkjum.

The window is exactly as wide as one image decode, which is why it shows up in a loaded test shard and almost never by hand.
records.translation: ``_MaskLoadWorker`` hefur þessa græju sem foreldri, svo án þessa eyðir eyðir skjásins QThread sem er enn að afkóða stóra TIFF-mynd, og Qt svarar því með ``qFatal("QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running")`` — kjarnaúttektarhrun, ekki undantekning. records.context: Every module that was built, not every module that was opened. A module is built the moment something asks this application view to point it at the open folder — :meth:`seed_folded` does, and so does any test or caller reaching for :meth:`folded_screen` — and pointing Model Compare at a folder starts a load independent execution path before its panel has ever been on application view. Walking the panels alone left those independent execution paths executing with nothing holding them, and the process died of it several actions later, in whatever happened to be executing when the memory behind them was touched.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.make_masks.MakeMasksScreen.close_folded#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: EVERY MODULE THAT WAS BUILT, not every module that was opened. A module is built the moment something asks this screen to point it at the open folder — :meth:`seed_folded` does, and so does any test or caller reaching for :meth:`folded_screen` — and pointing Model Compare at a folder starts a load thread before its panel has ever been on screen. Walking the panels alone left those threads running with nothing holding them, and the process died of it several actions later, in whatever happened to be running when the memory behind them was touched.
records.translation: HVERRI EININGU SEM VAR BYGGÐ, ekki hverri einingu sem var opnuð. Eining er byggð um leið og eitthvað biður þennan skjá að beina henni að opnu möppunni — :meth:`seed_folded` gerir það, og það gerir líka hver prófun eða kallandi sem sækir :meth:`folded_screen` — og að beina Model Compare að möppu ræsir hleðsluþráð áður en spjald hennar hefur nokkurn tíma verið á skjánum. Að fara eingöngu um spjöldin skildi þá þræði eftir í gangi án þess að neitt héldi í þá, og ferlið dó af því nokkrum aðgerðum síðar, í hverju því sem var í gangi þegar snert var við minninu á bak við þá.

records.context: Newer releases are then added. The wheel for a release cannot contain its own release note -- the note is written when the GitHub release is published, which is after that wheel is on PyPI -- so a bundled file is always one release behind the build carrying it. After the page is shown, :attr:`refresh_requested` asks the window to read the public releases list on a background execution unit, and :meth:`apply_releases` merges whatever comes back in front of the bundled list. Nothing here opens a socket: the panel only asks, and a fetch that fails, is rate-limited, is switched off in Preferences, or simply finds nothing newer leaves the bundled list exactly as it was drawn.

The wheel for a release cannot contain its own release note -- the note is written when the GitHub release is published, which is after that wheel is on PyPI -- so a bundled file is always one release behind the build carrying it. After the page is shown, :attr:`refresh_requested` asks the window to read the public releases list on a worker thread, and :meth:`apply_releases` merges whatever comes back in front of the bundled list. Nothing here opens a socket: the panel only asks, and a fetch that fails, is rate-limited, is switched off in Preferences, or simply finds nothing newer leaves the bundled list exactly as it was drawn.
records.translation: Nýrri útgáfum er síðan bætt við. Hjól (wheel) útgáfu getur ekki innihaldið eigin útgáfuskýringu -- skýringin er skrifuð þegar GitHub-útgáfan er birt, sem er eftir að hjólið er komið á PyPI -- svo meðfylgjandi skrá er alltaf einni útgáfu á eftir útgáfunni sem ber hana. Eftir að síðan er sýnd biður :attr:`refresh_requested` gluggann að lesa opinbera útgáfulistann á vinnuþræði, og :meth:`apply_releases` sameinar það sem kemur til baka fremst í meðfylgjandi listann. Ekkert hér opnar sökkul: spjaldið biður aðeins, og sókn sem bregst, er takmörkuð, er slökkt á í Preferences eða finnur einfaldlega ekkert nýrra skilur meðfylgjandi listann eftir nákvæmlega eins og hann var teiknaður.
